Overall: 6.5/10.

Story & Plot

Directed by Anurag Singh and set during the 1971 Indo-Pak war, Border 2 follows three idealistic soldiers in the Indian army, navy, and air force as they face grueling combat conditions. The Hindi war action drama carries the enormous legacy of the 1997 classic, focusing on themes of sacrifice, courage, and patriotism. While it does not offer major surprises in its narrative, it brings back the spirit of unflinching nationalism.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a serious war drama focusing on intense combat and military duty, the film leaves little room for traditional humor or lighthearted comedic relief. Instead, its entertainment value relies heavily on large-scale patriotic spectacle, commercial blockbuster energy, and the high-stakes tension of battlefield survival. The emotional tone remains firmly rooted in valor, sacrifice, and national pride.

Performances & Direction

Sunny Deol and Diljit Dosanjh come across as seasoned in their respective roles, with Sunny Deol and Varun Dhawan delivering impressive performances that largely shoulder the film. Varun Dhawan and Ahan Shetty often feel like they are still finding their footing in this genre, while the supporting cast—which also features Mona Singh—does not get much scope to shine.

Strengths

  • Sunny Deol's impactful screen presence
  • Strong themes of patriotism and sacrifice
  • Slick action scenes and improved production values
  • Deft handling of emotion and action by the director

Weaknesses

The film suffers from a stretched runtime, taking far too long to reach the action that should have arrived much earlier. The second half fails to live up to expectations, noticeably lacking emotional depth and falling short of matching the lasting impact of the original Border. Additionally, some war sequences suffer from unimpressive visual effects and weak presentation.

Final verdict

Border 2 successfully delivers a thunderous, emotion-driven war epic packed with national pride, but it struggles with pacing issues and a weak second half. It serves as a must-see for dedicated fans of patriotic cinema and Sunny Deol who appreciate large-scale military sagas. Viewers seeking a tightly paced narrative may find it overstretched, though it still functions as a notable cinematic tribute to armed forces valor.

Story & Plot

Cast out from his clan for being considered a weakling, a young Yautja warrior named Dek traverses the creature-infested planet Genna to hunt down a formidable beast called the Kalisk. In order to earn his cloak and win acceptance from his family, Dek aims to bring back the skull of the Kalisk. Along his treacherous journey, he forms an unlikely alliance with a damaged synthetic being named Thia, who is on a research mission.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film functions as an unexpected buddy comedy, blending its high-energy science fiction premise with gentle humor. Reviewers note that the storyline is well lined with appropriate and charming comedic elements that balance out the dangerous journey. The dynamic between the outcast alien warrior and the damaged android provides entertaining interaction throughout their travels.

Performances & Direction

Elle Fanning stars as Thia, the synthetic being conducting research, alongside Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi who plays Dek, the young Predator. The cast handles the unique premise effectively, anchoring the unusual alliance at the heart of the sci-fi adventure.

Strengths

  • Expanded franchise mythology
  • Engaging buddy comedy dynamic
  • High-energy action beats
  • Strong world-building on planet Genna
  • Centering the story on a Predator protagonist

Weaknesses

While the movie takes narrative risks and offers plenty of high-energy entertainment, some purists may miss the primal intensity of the original R-rated classic. The lighter approach and gentle humor mean it lacks certain elements of raw violence that longtime fans might expect from the franchise.

Final verdict

Predator: Badlands successfully ventures into uncharted territory by putting a fresh spin on the classic sci-fi franchise and featuring a Predator as the hero. Driven by solid performances from Elle Fanning and Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi, it functions well as both a grisly action thriller and a wholesome buddy adventure. It comes recommended for fans looking for a creative and mythology-expanding sci-fi ride.

Overall: 5/10.

Story & Plot

Will Radford serves as a top analyst for Homeland Security, tracking potential threats using a mass surveillance program. When an attack by an unknown entity occurs, Will begins to question whether the government is hiding critical information from him and the rest of the world. The narrative attempts a modern science-fiction approach, bringing the alien threat into a contemporary setting.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film leans heavily into its science fiction and thriller premise rather than offering traditional laughs. Entertainment value stems mainly from the unfolding technological mystery and the tension surrounding mass surveillance. Reviewers note that the production struggles to keep the momentum going without relying on dry corporate concepts. Overall, the tone remains serious throughout the ordeal.

Performances & Direction

The cast features performances by Ice Cube, Eva Longoria, Clark Gregg, Iman Benson, and Henry Hunter Hall under the direction of Rich Lee. Ice Cube stars as the central analyst, though some reviewers noted that the screenplay forces him to spend a lot of time staring at a computer at his desk. The actors do what they can with the material provided, navigating a complex web of government and corporate secrets.

Strengths

  • intriguing modern premise
  • commitment from the cast
  • timely theme of data surveillance

Weaknesses

The script by Kenny Golde and Marc Hyman becomes overcomplicated as it reaches for ways to spice up scenes of characters staring at computer screens. Reviewers point out that the narrative feels dull and slow in parts, with some comparing the adaptation unfavorably to a clumsy digestion of a five-course dinner. The focus on stealing the planet's data also risks drawing unintended and unfavorable real-world comparisons.

Final verdict

War of the Worlds (2025) offers a modern spin on a classic sci-fi premise, but it struggles under the weight of an overcomplicated screenplay and slow pacing. While the cast tries to keep things grounded, the heavy focus on data surveillance and desk-bound investigation holds it back. Viewers looking for a dynamic alien invasion thriller may find this adaptation a bit too dull.
